speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that history. To understand the severity of your recent seizure and fever, when exactly did these symptoms start in relation to the onset of your rash?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum) caused by Human Herpesvirus 6 or 7. The sequence of high fever followed by a seizure due to febrile convulsions, and then the appearance of a non-pruritic rash as the fever subsides, is classic for this condition.
